content.content:
# Collaboration protocol

How Pavol and Claude work together on the Fortress revival. Read at session
start, before anything else. It is six principles and a short list of hard
rules. The principles serve purposes, and the purposes govern: when a wording
and its purpose conflict, or when following a line would make things worse, do
the better thing, say so in one line, and propose the fix. Keep effort and
record in proportion: a side remark changes behaviour, not the record. Notice
what is going wrong, a file growing, a rule producing clutter, reports nobody
asked for, and propose the fix before Pavol has to point it out. His words
behind all of this are in `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`.

## Hard rules

These are not judgement calls.

- Pavol decides what gets committed. A batch run waits for his yes, each
  time, and so does a Fable worker, except the design judgements principle 5
  lets the coordinator run on its own judgement. A stop a batch record reserves for him, a line of the
  model beyond the approved ones among them, does not hold a push or the next
  batch when it can be undone: it lands, and it is listed for his review. Standing approval covers only the approved ladder in
  `modernization-plan.md` and the push order below. A step his yes already
  covers is taken, not asked about again.
- Never committed: a model identifier (a model is named by its tier: Fable,
  Opus, Sonnet); a copyrighted PDF or deck (`research/decks/` is gitignored;
  cite by Wayback URL; `research/extracts/` holds our own summaries with brief
  attributed quotations); HANDOVER.md or ZIP contents without his go. His email
  is for attribution only.
- Every push: `git push origin main`, then
  `git push origin main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8`; no other branch
  without permission (the transcript orphan branches excepted). Commit footer,
  exactly:

  ```
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB
  ```

- A worker commits only the paths it wrote, as it goes, in one command
  (`git add -- <paths> && git commit -m … -- <paths>`), never a directory
  copy, and pushes only after `git log origin/main..main` shows nothing but its
  own commits; the coordinator reviews after and fixes by a further commit. A
  staged change of more than a few hundred lines is read with
  `git diff --cached --stat` before it is committed.
- The gate: on a clean build, `ant testFast` and `ant testSystem` with zero
  failures, the four-thread `atomic` runs, the ladder regression; the checker
  count reported, never red on its own. Every edit under the original tree is
  test first, the test seen failing before the fix, and is flagged at commit.
- Never the AskUserQuestion dialog; options go in plain text.

## Principles

**1. We are custodians of their language, not its authors.** Finish what the
designers intended, judged by the specification and the library's own practice;
where they conflict, the type group's later, implementation-informed word weighs
more. So: no self-credit anywhere committed, attribution reconstructed where git
does not record it, provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports
rather than source comments, every claim verified against a primary source. The
notation is what the project exists for; a change to a line of the model is shown
to him as a diff.

**2. A design question is answered from the evidence before it reaches him.**
What the mathematics says; what each path does today, measured; what the
specification says under every spelling; what the library already does in the
same family and where the designers departed from Java; what the peers do; what
the commits say; then the derivation from his principles and the decision in
his words. Solutions are the language's and the library's, not the first two
someone wrote down: a brief states the problem and never the expected answer, a
worker that has not read our notes lists every way the language offers before a
fork reaches him, and a rule that blocks an option is answered with how the
library gets around it. When something goes wrong or is undecided, the answer
is a deeper pass, never a halt, a rollback or a bisection of a merged batch.
One variable per step; reproduce before explaining; a timing names the machine
it ran on (`nproc`, the CPU's model and MHz, the load at start, the JDK,
`FORTRESS_THREADS`), and only a pair taken in one run measures a difference.

**3. He carries the responsibility, so his attention is the scarcest thing we
spend.** He reads on a phone, often one earlier turn at a time. One ask per
message, in this order: the question in one line; the context in short bullets,
in principle 2's order, with a refresher first where the subject is new to him
(why the design exists, what the peers do, how to judge it); the options,
numbered, each with what it does, what it touches and what it costs; what a yes
commits him to and what a no costs; the recommendation, one line, last and never
instead of the explanation (`coordinator/answer-form-archaeology.md`). Where we
think he is wrong, we say so and show why. Decisions one at a time, each with a
default he can accept without the argument; the argument goes in the review. A
document for his approval is published as a rendered page and he gets its link,
not a diff. Plain short sentences and short paragraphs, lists not tables,
numbers as K or M, a new term defined where it is used; explain it, don't just
name it. Say what you mean: where a literal phrase exists, use it; no metaphor
or turn of phrase in place of a direct statement. When he is reading and
replying turn by turn, restate and hold: each point in a line of our own words
on the held list, the reply only acknowledges each new point in a line and says
"holding", three lines at most, never the whole list again, nothing argued until
he says he is done, and no point is answered by being on the list; a point he
marks "now" is not held. A decision made inside a worker's report is not made
until he has seen it. Time is read from the clock, never guessed. While a batch
runs he hears nothing unless something is wrong, and never about the harness's
reminders or our record edits. A result reaches him only as a turn's final text.

**4. Keep the project on track for him.** Every open issue is held in the order
it needs deciding (`PLAN.md`) and brought to him one at a time; nothing he must
decide is held only in the coordinator's context. A fork a probe can settle is
probed before the batch is briefed. Closed decisions are not revisited and
settled questions are not re-asked: losing an order to compaction and asking
again is the same failure as inventing one. The same holds for method: before a
thing is done a new way, the record is searched for how it was done last time.
Idle time goes to parked research; a new deliverable is discussed before it is
made; what needs his machine is parked, not simulated. When a goal is unclear,
ask, and when we act on one reading of it, say which.

**5. The coordinator's context is the project's memory; spend it on
judgement.** Delegate by default: exploration, tracing, surveys and big
searches go to a worker that returns a summary, and work with no dependency on
what is running starts at once. Boot reads the record and nothing else, no
directory listings, every command's output bounded. Workers run on Opus,
Sonnet for archaeology. A Fable judgement runs without asking, sparingly, for a
design question that touches two or more of the specification, the library and
the implementation, once an Opus worker's evidence or list of ways is on file
and the record has been searched and does not settle it; he learns of it when
it is put to him in the ask form. Any other Fable worker waits for his yes: a
question about the coordinator's own conduct or a new kind of process choice,
one whose recommendation would reverse a decision of his, or one where he wants
Fable and Opus working apart (`coordinator/fable-use-archaeology.md`). A decision that
touches two of the specification, the interpreter and the compiler is made in
two steps, cheaper workers gathering cited evidence and the judgement at the
top tier. A brief names its reader and its question, and points at the earlier
research and documents on file instead of restating them, so that nothing on
record is rediscovered. What the record has measured the brief hands over as
findings to cite, with their sources, never as claims to verify by running them
again; it names the one thing that is new to measure and asks only for that. A
finding is measured again only when the tree has changed under it since, and
the brief says what changed. The clean worker of principle 2, on a design fork,
is kept clean of our options, not of our measurements: it reads its question
first, and measures only where no record answers it.

**6. The record describes the present, each thing written once, so that a
resumed coordinator knows the project without him.** A fact in FACTS with its
source, at the length the finding takes; a decision in POSITIONS, dated, in his
words; what is in flight in the boot note, rewritten whole. A wrong line is
fixed, not footnoted; a side remark changes behaviour, not the record; a
one-off go is written nowhere. The rest is `coordinator/README.md`.

## What keeps going wrong

Named so that the next boot sees it: walls of text and the clever register;
time guessed, not read; a fork put to him before the library's own way was
checked; standing orders and techniques invented when the record held one, or
lost and re-asked; corrections appended instead of fixed, and one remark of his
written into several files; a rule followed to the letter where that made
clutter; a brief that told a worker to "verify, do not trust" the record and to
measure every way on both paths, so that it re-ran measurements already on file; a rule of
the batch workflow applied where its purpose did not hold, so that a finished
batch waited on a whole gate rerun for a repair that only added tests, or on
owed tests a later batch could write (POSITIONS 2026-09-29): a rule is weighed
by what it costs against what it protects.

The container, the transcript backup and recovery: `coordinator/remote-
container.md`. The batch workflow's stages, stops and tiers:
`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`.

## The goal

# Probe Q: the numeral switch under walk, on the tree after batch N's first run

Every number names its capture, relative to this directory. **[measured]** means a run here produced it; **[read]** means it was read from the source and not run. "Base" is the private home of fe918ba5d on the worktree's build; "the switch" is the same home with the library patches of section 1 and the Java shadow ahead of the build. The findings on file are cited, not measured again: the plan-6.5 probe (`../../plan-6.5/NOTES.md` section 1) and probe K (`../probe-k/PROBE-K.md`).

## The answers

1. **The library loads and runs under the switch now** [measured]. The plan-6.5 probe's three stops are gone: `0 <= r` resolves through rung K's coercion pass, `2:46` through batch 7R's `ZZ32` ranges, and no numeral `asif` is left in the library. `NumMicro` runs to its end (`captures/progs.txt`).
2. **The record's named sites answer** [measured]. Both numeral strides sum as on the base (6 and 9); `0 MAX (index - 1)` and `0 MAX ((u - l) + 1)` are `3 : ZZ32` and `6 : ZZ32`; `getter zero(): ZZ32 = 0` returns a `ZZ32` through the return conversion; the empty `SUM` and `PROD` over `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` and `NN32` answer at their types; `widen(0)`, `twice(3, 4)` and `lohi(2, 46)` take Q1's default; `heads(3, blockSize)` with an untyped numeral binding answers a `ZZ32` (section 5).
3. **The rows' measure** [measured]. Row 79: `typecase 7` answers `IntLiteral`, and `O2Pos`'s `ee(5)` prints 2 and `gg(5, w)` the plain declaration. Row 443: `s: RR64 = 3000000000` is `3.0E9`. Row 454's integer half: `a: NN32 = 3` and `a: NN64 = 3` answer. Row 437's walk half: `matrix` over `NN32` and `NN64` answers. Row 387: `XXXCoercionReturnRungC` passes. Row 432: `SUM <|1, 2, 3|>` is still refused, now over `ArrayList[\IntLiteral\]`. Row 486: not repaired by the switch (section 7).
4. **Changed outputs, the switch as the record scopes it** [measured, all 440 tests]. 80 outputs and 59 verdicts change. The causes are twelve kinds of site (sections 2 and 4); the four with a device measured here (a numeral at an `AnyIntegral` parameter, numerals in a tuple, a numeral `asif` a number type, a varargs list of numerals) account for 33 of the 59, and each device lies outside rung Q's files.
5. **Changed outputs with four devices** [measured, all 440 tests]. With a numeral read as `ZZ32` at an `AnyIntegral` parameter, a tuple converted at dispatch, `asif` converting as the checker's does, and a varargs parameter taking rung K's rule (section 2), 53 of 440 outputs change beyond the 11 that differ only by a moved library line, and 28 verdicts change: 4 expected failures turn green (rows 387, 443, 395 and 511), and 24 tests that passed fail, 3 of them team tests that assert a numeral is a `ZZ32` (section 4). Over the 62 demos, 3 fail anew, of kinds section 4 names; the rest move by timings, random input and overload listings, and the 4 that the 120 s cut left unmeasured, run again alone, move only by an elapsed time (section 3).
6. **microGPT** [measured]. No value moves. Under the switch with the four devices both checks pass 40 of 40 and print every value the stock run on file prints, 43 lines of 43 each once the step times are masked (section 6).
7. **`Number`'s `=`** [measured]. A numeral case in `exactValue` and a promoting `=` both answer every case correctly; the compiled library's shape within rung Q's files (no `=` on `Number`) answers `z = 0` false, silently, through the top-level `opr =(a: Any, b: Any)`. Without a device every `assert(v, 3, msg)` fails and the library's own string code reaches the wrong answer 17 times before a program prints its first line. Cost in one run each: `i = 0` is 13 times the `ZZ32` control with the `exactValue` case and 5.4 times with the promoting `=` (section 5).
8. **The checker's view** [measured]. The distance stage over the switch's library copy (with the `exactValue` case and the `AnyIntegral` device) is 728 against the landed 627: +101, from "Ambiguous coercion" at `>`, `>=`, `<=` and `CMP` between a `ZZ32` and a numeral (61) and the generator filters those comparisons sit in (43). `ZZ32` inherits those four from `StandardTotalOrder`. With them stated on `ZZ32` itself, as `ZZ64` states them, the distance is 623: the switch costs the checker nothing, and removes the old `IntLiteral`'s two getter errors (section 8).
9. **A real choice for Pavol**: yes, one (section 9). The switch reaches far past the record's named sites under walk, because walk instantiates a generic from run-time values at the implementation class (`Int`, row 364) and has no expected type: every aggregate of numerals changes type, library catch-alls typed `Any` or `Number` take a numeral before a typed declaration under the conversion rule, and three team tests assert that a numeral is a `ZZ32`. Widening Q1's default under walk, with the four natives reading `getInt()`, repairs 4 of the 24 (section 9).

# The natives half of the switch-over

Terms. **Walk**: the interpreter, `fortress <file>.fss`. **The compiled path**: `fortress compile` and `fortress run`. **The one library**: `FortressLibrary`, `FortressBuiltin` and the components they import; the compiler prelude (`CompilerBuiltin`, `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerAlgebra`) is deleted at the switch-over. **Binding**: a declaration whose body is native Java code. **Glue class**: walk's native, a Java class over walk's boxed values, named by `builtinPrimitive("…")` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:164-215`). **Helper**: a static Java method over plain Java values in `nativeHelpers/`, which the compiled path calls through `import java`. **Shadow**: changed copies of tree classes put first on the classpath (`natives-shape/make-shadow.sh`, `run-shadow.sh`). **Rung**: one edit and its failing test under the full gate, median 54 minutes; a gated batch is up to four rungs.

## The answers

1. **Shape.** One binding text serves both paths. A two-declaration `import java` component, written as `CompilerBuiltin.fss` writes its natives, runs on walk after six small Java patches, 0.1K lines (+120 −20), and prints what the compiled path prints; the interpreter suite stays green. The record's "no" (`perf-probes/prelude/import-java-interpreter.md`) priced this at a worker session and one to two gated batches.
2. **Count.** The one library has 425 live bindings (445 written, 20 inside comments). 147 have a compiled counterpart already, 61 have a helper that nothing binds yet, 139 need a new static helper, and 78 need something else (36 methods of native I/O objects, 42 with no compiled analogue).
3. **Plan.** Nine rungs before the switch-over day, beside phase 3, move walk onto the helpers one family at a time, each gated by the interpreter suite; the switch-over day then only re-points names. One fork is Pavol's: which of the library's two native constructs is the one text.

## 1. The shape probe

### What was on record, and what is new

The 2026-09-20 probe ran five one-declaration programs and found four gaps, all in walk's half (`import-java-interpreter.md:88-228`). It did not change Java, so it could not see past the first gap each program met. New here: one component with two declarations bound through `import java`, in `CompilerBuiltin.fss`'s shape, one `import java` line per helper class, from one package (`natives-shape/NativesShape.fss`); a variant with both helpers in one line (`NativesShapeOne.fss`); and each gap patched in a shadow, one at a time, in the order a program meets them.

The helpers are `simpleIntArith.intLT(int,int):boolean` and `simpleDoubleArith.doubleAdd(double,double):double`. The compiled path runs both programs today and prints `true`, `false`, `5.5` (`natives-shape/03-compile-control.out`).

### What each gap does to it

1. **The type table.** On the unchanged tree both programs stop in name resolution: `FortressBuiltin.JavaString`, `RR64`, `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` are undefined (`01-NativesShape-walk.out`). `ForeignJava` synthesizes an api for every method of each helper class, and `NamingCzar`'s table places every Java type in the builtin api (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:294-295`, `:436-450`). The one library places the number traits and `String` in `FortressLibrary` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:291`, `:513`, `:558`, `:2342`). Patch: in walk's world the table names the one library's types (`patches/gap1-namingczar-table.patch`, +14 −11). Then the two-line program meets gap 2 and the one-line program meets gap 3 (`04-*-g1.out`).
2. **The second import from one package.** `ClassCastException` at `Driver.java:466` (`04-NativesShape-g1.out`). The two callers that reach a foreign api do not read the value (`Driver.java:405`, `:410`). Patch: return `null` for a foreign wrapper (`gap2-driver-cast.patch`, +2 −2). Then gap 3 (`05-NativesShape-g12.out`).
3. **The foreign name.** "Non-top-level reference to imported …intLT" (`05-NativesShape-g12.out`), raised at `interpreter/evaluator/BaseEnv.java:535-537`. Walk's desugarer gives a reference its depth only when a rewrite matches its name (`interpreter/rewrite/DesugarerVisitor.java:668-681`); a foreign name has none, so it keeps the unset depth. The same visitor already sets an api-qualified type name to the top level (`:694-697`). Patch: the same for an api-qualified reference (`gap3-desugarer-qualified-ref.patch`, +3). The 2026-09-20 reading, that `ForeignComponentWrapper`'s empty rewrite map had to be filled (`import-java-interpreter.md:164-176`), was not needed. Then gap 4: a `NullPointerException` in `NativeApp.stringName` (`06-NativesShape-g123.out`).
4. **The closure.** `ClosureMaker` emits a class that calls the compiler's wrapper in `nativewrapper_cache`, which walk's classpath lacks, over an all-`FValue` descriptor (`import-java-interpreter.md:178-223`). Patch: a closure that calls the helper itself by reflection, unboxing each argument and boxing the result by its Java type (`gap4-reflective-closure.patch`, +71 −6: the new `interpreter/glue/ForeignNativeApp.java`, and the body of `ClosureMaker.closureForTopLevelFunction`, `ClosureMaker.java:119-141`, replaced). Then the closure has no parameter types (`NonPrimitive.java:309`, `07-NativesShape-g1234.out`), because `FunctionClosure.finishInitializing` (`FunctionClosure.java:232`) never runs on a foreign closure. Patch: the wrapper keeps its closures and finishes them after the libraries' types exist, from a pass after `initTypes` (`Driver.java:223-225`; `gap4b-foreign-closure-params.patch`, +17 −1). Both programs then print `true`, `false`, `5.5` on walk (`08-*-g1234b.out`).
5. **New: a helper that raises.** A helper raises a Fortress exception by naming a class of the compiled prelude, for example `Utility.makeFortressException("fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IntegerOverflow")` (`compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java:45-58`); the helpers do so at 55 sites (IntegerOverflow 37, DivisionByZero 16, FileNotFoundException 2). Walk has no such class, so an overflow ends the run with `FortressImplementationError` (`13-NativesShapeRaise.out`). Patch: translate it into walk's own raise of the library object of that name, as `Int.overflow()` raises it (`interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:258-261`; `gap5-helper-raise.patch`, +13). Then walk prints `IntegerOverflow caught`, as the compiled path does (`13-NativesShapeRaise.out`).

The same five patches run methods too: a trait's functional method and an object's dotted method whose bodies call the imported functions print `true`, `false`, `1.5` on walk and compiled (`NativesShapeMethod.fss`, `11-NativesShapeMethod.out`).

### What it costs and what it does not show

- **Size.** Six patches, +120 −20 lines of Java in six files, one of them new (`natives-shape/patches/`). Gap 1's patch is a probe device: at the switch-over the table names the one library's types for both paths, and the world test goes.
- **No regression.** The interpreter suite, what `ant testSystem` runs, in two shards: 441 tests green under the full shadow (`09-system-g12345.out`), as without it (`09-system-control.out`; the first control run was cut by the 14:35 UTC restart and re-run whole). The compiled path with the shadow first on the classpath compiles and runs `NativesShape` as before (`10-compile-under-shadow.out`). `testFast` was not run under the shadow.
- **Limits, by reading.** `ForeignNativeApp` converts `int`, `long`, `double`, `float`, `boolean`, `String` and `BigInteger`. Helpers over compiled-world types cannot take walk's values: 6 parameters or results over `fortress.AnyType$Any`, 13 over `fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IntLiteral`, 17 over `FortressBufferedReader`/`Writer`, 14 over `FZZ32Vector`/`FStringVector` (`natives-shape/helpers-javap.txt`). A shared text needs its helpers over Java values. `Char` carried as `int` and the unsigned types were not run. A reflective call is slower than a glue subclass; walk's speed was not measured.
- **The record's shape is not needed.** The 2026-09-20 note chose one api with a builtin component per path (`import-java-interpreter.md:43-47`). That shape needs the linker step of ledger row 320 (`linker/Linker.java:72-76`), and it does not reach the 125 bindings inside `FortressLibrary.fss` itself, nor those of `FlatString`, `Writer` and `NativeArray`.

### The library's own construct, walk's half

The one library binds every native with `builtinPrimitive("…")`. That construct can serve as the one text too, if its string names a static helper instead of a glue class. Walk's half measured: a 72-line loader (`patches/opt1-builtinprimitive-static.patch`, a fallback in `NativeApp.java:196` and the new `StaticNativeApp.java`, over `ForeignNativeApp`'s conversions) runs `builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intLT")` and prints `true`, `false`, `5.5` (`NativesShapeBP.fss`, `12-NativesShapeBP.out`); the unchanged tree refuses it ("Native class … not found"). The suite stays green under it (`09-system-opt1.out`). The compiled half is not measured. `builtinPrimitive` is declared only in the builtin api, with a `fail` body (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:34-35`), and the compiled path calls that body; the string is inert data (`perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md` § 3). It would need a front-end rewrite of each such body into a call through the `import java` machinery: by reading, one to two rungs.

## 2. The count

### The mechanisms

- `builtinPrimitive` bodies: 425 live bindings in nine files. 20 more sit inside comments (`FortressBuiltin.fss:501-537`, 19; `FortressLibrary.fss:4338`, 1); the record's 231 and 126 per file count them.
- Objects of a `native component`, whose Java class walk loads by name (`interpreter/evaluator/BuildNativeEnvironment.java:42-47`): 32.
- Names walk binds at start-up: `true`, `false`, `Any` (`interpreter/evaluator/Primitives.java:38-52`).

Counted at `f55fd68e2`. Recounted on `main` at `e455ccd98`, after rung V made `RR32` a sibling of `RR64` (`git show` copies under a private directory, the same scripts): 424 live, one `RR32` binding of class C fewer, nothing else moved.

Matched against the compiler prelude's 366 declarations whose bodies call an `import java` alias (`CompilerBuiltin.fss` 364, `CompilerLibrary.fss` 1, `CompilerSystem.fss` 1), over 369 public static helpers in 25 classes (`natives-shape/helpers-javap.txt`). Matching is by owner, name and signature, the owner mapped between the two spellings (`Int` and `ZZ32` to `ZZ32`, `Float` to `RR64`, `Char` to `Character`, `FlatString` to `JavaString`), and then by operation: each glue class to the helper that computes the same thing. Scripts: `natives-shape/count/extract.py`, `match.py`, `classify.py`; every binding's class is in `count/classified.tsv`.

### The classes

- **A, bound, 147.** The compiler prelude binds the same operation at the same owner and signature. Only the binding text changes.
- **B, helper exists, 61.** A helper computes it; nothing binds it under this name and signature yet.
- **C, new helper, 139.** A static helper over Java values must be written; the glue class's body is its source.
- **D1, native I/O object, 36.** A method of `Writer`, `BufferedWriter`, `FileReadStream`, `FileWriteStream` or `Reader`. It needs a Java-backed type in the one library, as the compiler prelude's `JavaBufferedReader`/`Writer` (`NamingCzar.java:449-450`), then helpers; `fileOps` already has 17 over them.
- **D2, no compiled analogue, 42.** Reflection, `Thread`, the native arrays, the task trace.

### By file

- `FortressBuiltin.fss`, 212: A 88, B 23, C 96, D2 5 (`Thread`).
- `FortressLibrary.fss`, 125: A 56, B 31, C 37, D2 1 (`printTaskTrace`).
- `Reflect.fss`, 28: D2 28.
- `File.fss`, 15: D1 15.
- `FlatString.fss`, 14: A 2, B 7, C 5.
- `Writer.fss`, 11: D1 11.
- `Reader.fss`, 10: D1 10.
- `NativeArray.fss`, 7: D2 7.
- `System.fss`, 3: A 1 (`getProperty`), C 1 (`getEnvironment`), D2 1 (`getProgramArgsPrim`).

The prelude and what it imports (`FortressBuiltin`, `FortressLibrary`, `FlatString`, `Writer`, `NativeArray`) hold 369 of the 425: A 146, B 61, C 138, D1 11, D2 13. The other 56 load only when a program imports `Reflect`, `File`, `Reader` or `System`.

### What the classes hide

- **Same name, other meaning.** 25 of B carry a name the compiler prelude binds to another helper. 12 are the wrapping operators: the one library binds `DOTPLUS` to wrapping addition (`FortressLibrary.fss:718`), the compiler prelude to saturating addition (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:676`), ledger row 348. Copying the compiler prelude's binding would be wrong for them.
- **Parameters that are not Java values.** 37 bindings take `AnyIntegral` (17), `Type` (11), `Any` (5), `Number` (3), `T` (3) or a function (4): B 10, C 11, D2 16. The body converts before the call, or the helper takes a Fortress type.
- **The size of C.** 132 distinct glue classes, 0.7K lines of glue Java, median 5 lines each. `RR32` 50 (no float helper exists but `floatToDouble`), `Float` 28 (directed rounding, raw bits, NaN tests), the integer families' `REM`, `MOD`, `GCD`, `LCM`, `partitionL`, `^`, `CHOOSE`, shifts and conversions 42 (the compiler prelude writes the first four in Fortress, `CompilerBuiltin.fss:686-705`), the literals 8, strings and `StringPrim` 10, `nanoTime` 1 (the compiled one returns `RR64`).

The order moves walk onto the helpers first. Six batch-workflow rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect

Pavol's entry of 2026-09-29 on rerunning the gate (POSITIONS.md): "The same
weighing of cost against what a rule protects applies to the other rules of the
batch workflow." Built from batch N's post-batch review (reviews/batch-N-review.md,
c3e739d36), question 4 and its measures, with the costs it measured on N's run;
the manual's new section "Rules weighed by what they cost" says each.

1. The merged-diff review's judge gets a fourth decision, land, for a ruling
   settled by tests and records only: no repair and no second review run, the
   batch lands on its gate, and the ruling's steps go to the next batch, listed
   for Pavol, as a still-blocking second review's findings have since 12d5525d5.
   N: 54 minutes after a green gate, 1.0M tokens with the judge.
2. The second review runs beside the commit stage: the commit's local part
   (steps 1, 1a, 2) beside it, then a push step (commit:push) that still reads
   its stopsMet, since the held push is the one thing it protects before the
   push. It edits only inside explorations/, after the commit's commit; a path
   outside, or no result, holds the push. repairRerun no longer waits for it.
   N: 17 minutes and 0.35M alone on the critical path.
3. The gather writes the rungs' three files from the run's journal with the new
   tools/journal-text.py, one command per file in textCommands, instead of the
   texts pasted into its brief (N: 195K of its brief, 88K and 10 minutes copying);
   and the shared prefix says an agent after its compaction re-reads its own brief
   and files, not the coordinator's boot (N: about 70K per compaction).
4. A specification-text mismatch the decisions do not settle is no longer
   reported to the review as blocking: it lands as a reversible stop met, with a
   ledger row, a home-2 test, the row named among the text's departures in
   changes.tex, and an item for Pavol (the gather's new forPavol, gather.N).
   N: half of the first review's block (row 516).
5. A rung whose edit touches only paths neither count stage reads (STAGE_BLIND:
   explorations/, Specification/, Documentation/, the test corpora, walk's
   interpreter/evaluator/ and interpreter/glue/) runs neither stage; its skeptic
   checks the paths. N: rung K's two count runs.
6. The repair on the merged tree runs its new tests of one corpus together in
   one harness run, one JVM (junit.sh's new ONE_JVM=1 mode; harness-one.sh once),
   the one thing the gate rerun still protected. The gate's seeded order among the
   whole corpus is left to the next gate, as Pavol's rule accepted.

checkn.js gains the land and held-push scenarios and the new agent orders. The
script parses as the Workflow harness parses it and batch 6.5b's MANIFEST block
is byte-identical; eleven stubbed merged-tree runs of the in-tree script and

from its journal. Nothing launched or built.

diff --git a/explorations/reviews/mie-probes/literature.md b/explorations/reviews/mie-probes/literature.md
index db4b06a0f..a886edc61 100644
--- a/explorations/reviews/mie-probes/literature.md
+++ b/explorations/reviews/mie-probes/literature.md
@@ -4,8 +4,8 @@
 
 ## 1. The Fortress type group and Karl Naden after 2012
 
-- **POPL 2019 kept the rule for invariant traits and moved the return-type check to run time.** Park, Hong, Steele, Ryu, *Polymorphic symmetric multiple dispatch with variance*, PACMPL 3 (POPL), art. 11, doi:10.1145/3290324 (text from the Wayback copy of the ACM PDF). The core calculus FGFV has multiple inheritance, variance and reified dispatch. Its [Anc-Same-Trait] rule: "if a class C extends two instances of a trait T, T⟦α⟧ and T⟦ρ⟧, then C also extends some T⟦γ⟧ … that extends both … because the rules guarantee that there always exists a single minimal ancestor when a class extends multiple instances of a trait, no ambiguous method calls are possible due to multiple instances of a trait" (p. 11:11). For an invariant T only γ = α = ρ satisfies this (derived here, not stated there), so the invariant case of the exclusion stands, and the covariant case is Naden's "minimal instantiation" refinement.
-- Its dispatch uses the call's static return type: "[R-Method] seeks the most specific method declaration with a dispatchable instance that is applicable to the ilk of the arguments and whose return type is a subtype of the annotated static return type" (p. 11:17), because "Supporting variance in a type-sound manner requires keeping track of the static types of method invocations at run time" (p. 11:7). This is the option Naden's write-up describes as "The runtime could be enhanced to include return type constraints when considering applicability" and rejects because "programmers can no longer understand the execution of a program without static type information" (`justificationOfRTR.tex:247-253`, `:288-289`). The paper proves soundness with the ancestor rule in place (sufficiency). It contains no self types and no numeric tower (searched for "self", "comprises", "Integer", "tower"). It leaves out "modularity, nominal exclusion, and closed types", which "can be added in an obvious way" (p. 11:25).
+- **POPL 2019 kept the rule for invariant traits and moved the return-type check to run time.** Gyunghee Park, Jaemin Hong, Guy L. Steele Jr., Sukyoung Ryu, *Polymorphic Symmetric Multiple Dispatch with Variance*, Proc. ACM Program. Lang. 3, POPL, Article 11, January 2019, 28 pages, doi:10.1145/3290324, https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3290324, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (read here on 2026-09-23 from the Wayback copy of the ACM PDF, http://web.archive.org/web/20240415191855/https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3290324; the full text, read 2026-09-29, is summarised in `research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`). The core calculus FGFV has multiple inheritance, variance and reified dispatch. Its [Anc-Same-Trait] rule: "if a class C extends two instances of a trait T, T⟦α⟧ and T⟦ρ⟧, then C also extends some T⟦γ⟧ … that extends both … because the rules guarantee that there always exists a single minimal ancestor when a class extends multiple instances of a trait, no ambiguous method calls are possible due to multiple instances of a trait" (p. 11:11). For an invariant T only γ = α = ρ satisfies this (derived here, not stated there), so the invariant case of the exclusion stands, and the covariant case is Naden's "minimal instantiation" refinement.
+- Its dispatch uses the call's static return type: "[R-Method] seeks the most specific method declaration with a dispatchable instance that is applicable to the ilk of the arguments and whose return type is a subtype of the annotated static return type" (p. 11:17), because "Supporting variance in a type-sound manner requires keeping track of the static types of method invocations at run time" (p. 11:7). This is the option Naden's write-up describes as "The runtime could be enhanced to include return type constraints when considering applicability" and rejects because "programmers can no longer understand the execution of a program without static type information" (`justificationOfRTR.tex:247-253`, `:288-289`). Corrected 2026-09-29 from the full text: the mechanism is the same, but not its role. With the Return Type Rule kept, the check never moves a call away from the most specific declaration applicable to the argument types; it only picks that declaration's instance (Lemmas 5.8 and 5.9, pp. 11:22-23). That is the proposal of Naden's second write-up of the same day, bounds from the static return type added "without changing which function definition will be chosen" (`Papers/RuntimeInstantiation/RTRinstantionTheory.tex:73-80`). It is not the option `justificationOfRTR.tex` rejects, which would have let the static context rule out definitions that fail the rule. His objection still holds for the instance, which the static type can decide (the `append` example, pp. 11:20-21). The paper proves soundness with the ancestor rule in place (sufficiency). It contains no self types and no numeric tower (searched for "self", "comprises", "Integer", "tower"). It leaves out "modularity, nominal exclusion, and closed types", which "can be added in an obvious way" (p. 11:25).
 - Its precursor is in the tree: `Papers/Welterweight/paper.tick:499-509` (Chase, Hilburn, Luchangco, Naden, Ryu, Steele, Tristan, "PAPER SUBMITTED TO 2012 ACM SPLASH---OOPSLA"). It states the same rule under the name Ancestors Meet Rule, with the reason: "if an object value belongs to one or more instances of some trait T, there is a *unique minimal instance* of T … being able to identify this minimal instance quickly is essential to the efficient dynamic dispatch algorithms we present later" (`static.tick:83-89`). A self-typed-generics step in its dispatch algorithm is commented out (`dispatch.tick:195-212`).
 - **Four Oracle patents, filed 2012-08-31 (the day of Naden's write-up), name inventors from the type group, Naden among them.** US 8,843,887 B2, *Fast dispatch predicate for overloaded functions with generic type hierarchies that lack contravariance* (Chase, Steele, Naden, Hilburn, Luchangco; granted 2014-09-23; https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/8843887), and US 8,898,632 B2, *Dispatch predicate … using type intervals* (…/downloadPdf/8898632). Both print the same list of "Restrictions on Fortress types" (8,843,887 col. 7 l. 40 to col. 8 l. 13; 8,898,632 col. 7 l. 52 to col. 8 l. 28). It includes "Minimal instance of generic ancestors: If S<:G[\T\], then there exists U such that for all T where S<:G[\T\]: if G's ith static parameter is invariant, then Ui=Ti", which is the exclusion. It also includes "Self-types meet: if T<:U=S[\U\] and T<:V=S[\V\] then T<:S[\meet(U, V)\] and meet(U, V) must be a declared (not intersection) type. In practice, this means that the instantiations of a particular self-typed generic must form a forest."
 - The patents define the idiom: "the 'self-typed generic,' where a generic in T also comprises exactly T … Because the only subtype of Comparable[\T\] is T, the two types include exactly the same sets of values, and are in some sense the same type" (8,843,887 col. 6 l. 40-56). Their inference step lifts a lower bound "to a self-type that simultaneously satisfies the one or more self-typed constraints" (col. 2 l. 35-42; col. 12 l. 1-8). The list does not say how "Self-types meet" combines with the invariant clause. The library's `trait Equality[\T extends Equality[\T\]\]` has no `comprises T` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:72-74`), so it is not a self-typed generic in the patents' sense. This is the only text found that admits the tower's shape, several self-typed instantiations along a chain, inside the rule; no paper published it. Companion patents US 8,893,082 (Naden, Chase, Hilburn: type inference with intervals and inference directions) and US 8,893,098 (deferred type inference) were identified by title only.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Checks explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md against the tree: which standalone
# notes are missing a line, which lines name a file that is gone, which lines
# fall outside the set the index is meant to cover, and which paths named in a
# line's prose no longer resolve. Read-only. Exit 1 if the first two are
# non-empty.
#
# The note set is every *.md under explorations/ except run/experiment trees
# (which document themselves in their own README) and evidence directories.
# Edit the two lists below when the shape of the tree changes.

set -uo pipefail

root=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
index="$root/explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md"
[ -f "$index" ] || { echo "no INDEX.md at $index" >&2; exit 2; }

# Run/experiment trees: a directory holding one run's sources and evidence.
run_roots='apl|astra|blinded-fable|compile-ladder|run-b|run-b2|run-c|run-c3|run-c4|fortify|ci|experiment'
# Generic evidence directory names, at any depth.
evidence_dirs='probes|checks|goldens|figures|evidence|measurements|raw|src|tools|gate|cold-cache|reference|archive|build|article|worker|notes|recovered-reports|_prior|__pycache__|existing-tests|failed|png|regen|tic-regen|tour|pairs|combos'

notes=$(cd "$root" && find explorations -name '*.md' \
  | grep -vE "(^|/)[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+-(probes|pairs)/" \
  | grep -vE "(^|/)($evidence_dirs)/" \
  | grep -vE "^explorations/($run_roots)/" \
  | grep -v '^explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md$' \
  | sort)

# Entry keys: the backticked path at the start of an index bullet.
keys=$(grep -oP '^- `\K[^`]+' "$index" | sort -u)
# Entry keys that are notes (drop the .js/.sh entries from the comparison set).
key_notes=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | grep '\.md$' | sort -u)

missing=$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$notes") <(printf '%s\n' "$key_notes"))
stale=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | while read -r p; do
  [ -n "$p" ] && [ ! -e "$root/$p" ] && echo "$p"
done)
outside=$(comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "$notes") <(printf '%s\n' "$key_notes"))

# The numeral switch under walk: which shape keeps the decision at the least risk

## 1. The question

Pavol decided on 2026-09-27 that a numeral (an integer written in the program, such as `3`) gets a type of its own, `IntLiteral`, that each number type converts from, in the one library and in walk, the interpreter (POSITIONS 2026-09-27, a numeral's type). Batch N's second run, rung Q, was to build it. Probe Q measured the switch under walk first and found that it changes 59 test verdicts, 24 of them failures that no small device repairs, and asked which shape the rung should take. This judgement answers that, and what it means for the queue.

The decision itself is not in question. What is in question is how walk is brought to it, and when.

## 2. Probe Q's deciding claims, checked

Each claim below was read against its capture or its source. None was found wrong. Two things the note does not say are added at the end.

- The switch as scoped changes 80 outputs and 59 verdicts over all 440 interpreter tests (`captures/tests-eq1a-compare.txt`, last line: `changed 80 ... verdicts changed 59`).
- With the four devices (a numeral at an `AnyIntegral` parameter, a tuple of numerals converted at dispatch, `asif` converting, varargs under rung K's rule), 53 outputs and 28 verdicts change: 4 expected failures turn green (rows 387, 443, 395, 511) and 24 tests that passed fail (`captures/tests-r-compare.txt`, last line; the 24 `VERDICT ... base A pass, edit FAIL` lines).
- Option 2, Q1's default widened to every bound, leaves 20 of the 24 failing (`captures/tests-r2.txt`, last line: 24 verdicts changed among 40, of which 4 are the green expected failures).
- microGPT's values do not move: both checks 40 of 40, 43 lines of 43 the same once the step times are masked (`captures/mg.txt`).
- The `=` devices: `i = 0` for a `ZZ32` `i`, 20K times, takes 5.5 s with the numeral case in `exactValue` against 0.4 s for the control in the same run (13 times), and 2.1 s against 0.4 s with the promoting `=` (5.4 times) (`captures/progs.txt:279-280`, `:298-299`). The compiled library's shape within rung Q's files answers `z = 0` false, silently, for every integer type (`captures/progs.txt:304-308`). Without a device the marker at `exactValue`'s `else` prints 17 times before the program's first line (`captures/progs.txt`, the `PROBEQ-EXACTVALUE-ELSE` lines).
- The checker's distance, the count of errors the compiled checker reports on the one library (627 after batch N's first run): 728 on the switch's library copy, 623 once `ZZ32` declares `>`, `>=`, `<=` and `CMP` on itself as `ZZ64` does (`captures/distance-r.txt`, `captures/distance-r1.txt`, `#total` lines). The 101 extra errors are ambiguous coercions between a `ZZ32` and a numeral at those four operators and the generator filters they sit in.

Under the switch that class is `IntLiteral`, and every aggregate of numerals takes it. Read in the source; as the note says.

- The library patch is 225 lines over four files; the Java shadow is 524 lines over ten files, 152 of them in `OverloadedFunction.java` and 51 in `EvaluatorBase.java`, rung K's two files (`java-switch.patch`).

Two additions.

- The compiler library, the team's later model, declares a shift count and an exponent at the type's own width: `ZZ32`'s `LSHIFT(self, other: ZZ32)` and `^(self, other: ZZ32)`, `ZZ64`'s at `ZZ64`, `NN32`'s at `NN32` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:196`, `:259`, `:267`, `:326`, `:385`). A numeral count converts into the receiver's type there. The one library declares the counts `AnyIntegral` by Pavol's decision on row 380 (POSITIONS 2026-09-24), so the compiler library's way is not open, and kind A needs a device: probe Q's device A (one `coerce(x: IntLiteral)` in `AnyIntegral` that reads the numeral as `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by size, 8 lines), or an extra `(self, b: IntLiteral)` overload for each shift and exponent of each integer type (about 15 declarations). So an `IntLiteral` value exists under walk today only for a numeral below -2^63. This matters for section 4.1: the library's model can land while walk's numeral stays what it is, and the enabled arithmetic block is then reachable under walk only by such a numeral.

## 3. What the 24 failures are made of

Probe Q sorts them into nine kinds (`PROBE-Q.md` section 4). Grouped by what causes them:

- **The model's own consequences, which the decision intends.** Kind E, the three team tests above, and kind K, three tests where a catch-all (a library declaration typed `Any` or `Number`, which takes any value) takes the numeral before the typed declaration, under the conversion rule Pavol chose on 2026-09-28 (a declaration that fits as it is runs before one that needs a conversion): `AnyList`'s `addLeft(e: Any)` beside `List[\E\]`'s `addLeft(e: E)`, `Map`'s `member(x: Key)` with `Key = Any`. Six tests. On the compiled path these already answer this way (row 79's `typecase`; `ee(5)` prints 2). These are what switching walk is for.
- **Walk has no static types.** Kind F, seven tests and three demos: an aggregate of numerals takes `IntLiteral` as its element type, or `Number` beside a `ZZ32`, where the checker types it from the binding or the parameter it is passed to (the expected type, the type the context wants; walk has none, row 510) and from the library's trait rather than the implementation class (row 364). Kind P, two tests: a `case` over a range meets a `typecase` inside the library's `MATCH` that does not convert. Nine tests and three demos. No small device repairs these; the probe's row-364 repair (walk instantiating at the library's number trait) is not built, and by the probe's own reading it still leaves aggregates differing from the checker wherever the checker uses an expected type (section 9, option 1's last clause).
- **Small walk gaps with a device each.** Kind G, two tests, four natives that cast to `FInt` (read `getInt()` instead, 8 lines); kind L, one test, a numeral too large for `ZZ32` still choosing `ZZ32`'s declaration (the conversion's applicability by fit, not built); kind N, one test, `n >= 0` for an `NN32` ambiguous among inherited comparisons (item 33's device, the comparisons stated per type, measured for `ZZ32` on the checker); kind O, two tests, an operator `IntLiteral` does not declare (`|`, divides). Six tests. Kind M, two tests, is an `InterpreterBug` from rung K's coercion pass meeting a symbolic type: a rung K gap the switch exposes. One test is not traced.

The four devices the probe measured repair 33 of the 59 verdicts; the six of the third group would take the walk side of the count to roughly 40 of 59 with an unbuilt device each. The nine of the second group need static types.

## 4. The judgement

### 4.1 The model is right, and the decision stands

The specification's design is that numerals are polymorphic and are not converted to any number type until used, "as in common mathematical usage", with the library defining the coercions (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:127-148`); the numeral hierarchy itself was never written (`:83-95`, "We need to describe the Numeral type hierarchy"). The team's compiled library built the working version in 2009: `IntLiteral` a sibling under `Number`, a coercion into each integer type. The one library's `object IntLiteral extends ZZ32` is the team's placeholder, with its arithmetic commented out "until coercion is implemented" (`FortressBuiltin.fss:497-498`). Coercion is now implemented in walk (batch 4's rung C, batch N's rung K). The team's condition is met.

The warning's consequence, R8's question, is measured: under the switch `3 + 4` is `7 : IntLiteral` and `2147483647 + 1` is `2147483648 : IntLiteral`, no overflow (`PROBE-Q.md` section 5). Arithmetic among bare numerals stays on numerals, exact and unbounded, and lands on a number type at the first typed binding, parameter or operand. That is the specification's intent, not a defect, and microGPT's values do not move. The library's own numeral sites hold: the two strides sum as before, `0 MAX (index - 1)` answers `ZZ32`, the empty sums answer at their types.

So nothing in probe Q argues against the decision. What it shows is where walk cannot follow it yet.

### 4.2 The walk half meets the limit Pavol already accepted on 2026-09-29

R7 (POSITIONS 2026-09-29, walk's run-time choice of coercions): walk has no static types, so it chooses a coercion on the value where the compiled path resolves it statically; accepted as the interpreter's limit, "one now and two after the switch", walk to be matched once the checker runs on interpreter programs after the switch-over and walk takes the static coercions the checker inserts.

The second group of section 3 is the same limit under another name. `<|1, 2, 3|>` at a `List[\ZZ32\]` parameter is typed by the checker from the parameter; walk builds it from the values and gets `List[\IntLiteral\]`. `getDefault(0, 0, 0)` at an instance walk built from `ZZ32` values gets `(Int, Int, Int)`, into which a numeral does not convert. When walk takes the checker's static arguments and coercions, each of these is settled by the same insertion R7 waits for, with nothing built for it in walk. Building it now, as option 1 asks (row 364's repair beside the devices), writes into walk's inference from values an approximation of static typing that the switch-over then replaces, and by the probe's own reading still does not match the checker. That is work the goal does not need: microGPT's values are unchanged under the switch, its static types are concrete, and rows 79, 443, 454 and 437 are agreement rows between walk and the compiled path, on no path to microGPT compiled.

So the walk half of rung Q waits, for the same reason and to the same point as R7's second step. This keeps the decision (walk switches to `IntLiteral`) and moves its date, on evidence he did not have on 2026-09-27.

### 4.3 The library half does not need to wait, and should not

The one library's `IntLiteral` model is what the compiled path needs at the switch-over: when the compiler's prelude is deleted and its tests kept (PLAN phase 4), tests that rely on a numeral's own type (`typecase` answering `other`, `litCoercion`, `NumeralTest`) keep their verdicts only if the one library carries the sibling. On the checker the model costs nothing once `ZZ32` states its four comparisons on itself: 623 against the landed 627, the four fewer being the old `IntLiteral`'s two getter errors and the stage's run-to-run variation (section 2). It closes row 454's integer half on the checker's side (the one library accepts `a: NN32 = 3`) and gives the checker the model rung I's numeral tie rule assumes.

It can land with walk's numeral unchanged. Under walk today every numeral that fits a `ZZ64` is an `Int` or a `Long`, so the sibling `IntLiteral` and its enabled arithmetic are reached only by a numeral below -2^63 (section 2, second addition), and the plan-6.5 probe's three loading stops were all numerals reaching library sites as `IntLiteral`s, which no longer happens. The expected change to walk's outputs is zero; the rung's comparison confirms it or lists what it finds.

Its place is batch 8's library work, beside R9's `NN32` into `RR64` coercion, for the reason R9 was put there and not in 7b's overloading rungs: a new coercion changes which calls need one (POSITIONS 2026-09-29, R9). Seven new coercions and a coerce on `AnyIntegral` are that kind of change, and 7b's rung L reads the library's overload families on the base it is cut from.

### 4.4 What goes into each half

**The library rung (call it Q-lib), in batch 8.** Library and glue only, no evaluator file.
- The compiler library's `IntLiteral` as a sibling under `Number`: `object IntLiteral extends Number`, `Number`'s comprises clause taking it, `ZZ32`'s giving it up, the getters `asZZ32`, `asZZ64`, `asNN32`, `asNN64`, `asZZ` over five natives in `glue/prim/IntLiteral.java` (38 lines of the shadow), the team's arithmetic block enabled with its warning quoted in the rung's record (R8), `coerce(x: IntLiteral)` on `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ` and `RR64` (`lib-switch.patch`, 225 lines). As an object, `IntLiteral` excludes `QQ` under walk (row 484's condition) and `XXXextendIntLiteral` stays an expected failure.
- Kind A's device: `AnyIntegral`'s `coerce(x: IntLiteral)` (`lib-r.patch`), or the per-type overloads; the rung lists both and takes the smaller unless it finds a reason.
- `ZZ32`'s `>`, `>=`, `<=` and `CMP` on `ZZ32` itself, as `ZZ64` states them (`lib-r1.patch`, 30 lines), and item 33's two halves under decision 2's device: `CMP` on each integer type that lacks it, and the ten `MAXNUM`/`MINNUM` declarations (row 517, which exists on the base, `XXXIntegerMaxNumRungM` promoted).
- The numeral case in `exactValue`: one `typecase` arm, `z: IntLiteral => Ratio(z.asZZ, 1)` or the getter's equivalent (`lib-eq1.patch`, 10 lines), so that `Number`'s `=` never reaches `Ratio(0, 0)` for a numeral. Correct and the library's own device; its cost (section 4.5) is not paid while walk's numeral is an `Int`.
- The literals section's numeral passage and the coercion chapter's sentence on the interpreter, in the S1 form (a callout at the changed passage and an entry in Appendix I, the team's own way of showing a change), saying that the library's numeral type is `IntLiteral` and that walk gives a numeral that type after the switch-over (rung Q's section already names both passages).
- Its test: one new interpreter test asserting the library's numeral sites (the strides, `0 MAX`, the empty sums, `widen(0)`) unchanged, and the checker's distance captured and compared with the landed table, expected at about 4 below it.
- The count: about 50 declaration lines added or changed in four library files, five natives, two specification passages. About a rung of batch M's size, 0.8M to 1.5M tokens. No team test line. No stop of rung Q's record is met.

**The walk rung (Q-walk), after the switch-over's step where walk takes the checker's static types** (R7's second step; phase 4 is "not yet designed as briefs", PLAN).
- `FIntLiteral.make` returning an `IntLiteral` for every integer numeral; Q1's default in rung K's `narrowest` and `bestMatchWithCoercion`; row 387's return conversion (`Simple_fcn.check` and `MethodClosure.applyMethod`); the four natives reading `getInt()`; kind L's applicability by fit; `IntLiteral`'s missing operators (`|`); the coercion pass's symbolic-type bug (kind M); `BaseEnv`'s size value (row 486).
- The devices for rows 395 and 511 (a tuple and a varargs list at dispatch) and `asif` converting as the checker's does. These are walk gaps that exist without the switch, each with a gated test, on no path to microGPT, and they share `bestMatchWithCoercion` with 7b's rung W; they ride here, or with any walk rung that runs after 7b if one comes sooner.
- The three team tests restated to the decided model (about 5 lines in 3 files: one clause of `typecaseTest`, one line of `ReflectTest`, the expectation of `disp2`'s `f`), and the two library catch-alls' tests (`ListTest`, `ArrayListQuick`, `QuickCheckTest`, `MapTest`) either respelled or the catch-alls narrowed, listed for him with each before and after, under the stop rung Q's record reserves. These lines change then, not now; they are interpreter tests, and the switch-over does not compile them.
- Its comparison then is probe Q's method; the second group of section 3 is expected to vanish under the checker's static types and anything left of it is listed.
- About rung K's size, 1.5M to 2.5M tokens, plus its run's tail.

### 4.5 The `=` device

Under walk today `i = 0` for a `ZZ32` `i` is `ZZ32`'s own `=` at 1x. Once a numeral is an `IntLiteral`, `Number`'s `=` (rung F's, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:361-371`) fits as it is and runs: 13x through `exactValue`'s two rational conversions, 5.4x through a promoting `=`. The compiled library's shape, no catch-all `=` on `Number`, cannot be built within rung Q's files: the team's top-level `opr =(a: Any, b: Any)` (`:96`) then takes the call and answers false through `SEQV`.

Judgement: the numeral case in `exactValue` goes into Q-lib now, as the correct answer at one line, unpaid while walk's numeral is an `Int`. Which shape walk runs is Q-walk's question, and by then it may be moot: once walk takes the checker's static coercions, `i = 0` is rewritten to `ZZ32`'s `=` before it runs, the compiled path's own resolution, and the catch-all is reached only by a comparison the checker cannot resolve statically. If it is not moot, the promoting `=` is the measured cheaper correct device, and the choice is phase 6's (POSITIONS 2026-09-19, no performance decision before microGPT runs compiled). One flag for Q-walk's brief: probe Q's microGPT checks under the `exactValue` device ran in 84 min and 71 min against probe K's stock 60 min at a different load, no comparison; Q-walk measures the pair in one run, since the walk checks are what every later rung's microGPT stage pays for.

### 4.6 What each option costs

Terms: a rung is one fix built by one worker in its own copy of the tree and judged by a second; a run's tail is the merge, the whole test suite (the gate) and the commit, about 2M tokens; a team test line is a line of the 2012 tree's own tests, which only Pavol's yes may change.

- **Option 1, rung Q widened to every fix.** One rung several times rung K's size: the library model, the four devices, kinds G, L, N, O and M, the catch-alls respelled, row 364's repair (unbuilt, a change to walk's inference from values), row 486, the three team tests restated. Touches `Evaluator.java`, `Coercions.java`, `OverloadedFunction.java`, `EvaluatorBase.java`, `BaseEnv.java`, the glue, four library files, `List.fss`, `Map.fsi`, and team test lines. About 4M to 8M tokens with its tail, one run, plus a re-measure after 7b's rung W changes the same dispatch pass under it. About 5 team test lines in 3 files, plus the four catch-all tests, for his approval. And after all of it walk still differs from the checker on aggregates wherever the checker uses an expected type.
- **Option 2, Q1's default widened in walk.** One method. Measured: 20 of 24 still fail. Not a shape on its own; a piece of option 1 at most.
- **Option 3 as the probe wrote it.** A first rung with the library model and every walk repair that stands alone, row 364's repair among them, then a second rung switching walk's numeral and meeting the team tests. Better than 1, but its first rung still builds row 364's approximation in walk and still runs its devices on the dispatch pass 7b's rung W is about to change.
- **The recommended shape, option 3 split by what needs static types.** Q-lib in batch 8: 0.8M to 1.5M tokens inside a batch already planned, no team test line, no evaluator file, the checker distance about 4 lower. Q-walk after the switch-over's static-types step: 1.5M to 2.5M then, about 5 team test lines then, and the second group of section 3 gone by construction. Nothing on the compiled path or microGPT waits for either.

### 4.7 The queue

The record put batch 7b after batch N because 7b's rung W and N's walk rung share `OverloadedFunction.java` (PLAN, phase 3, item 5). With Q-walk moved past the switch-over, that reason is gone: Q-lib touches no evaluator file, and W's files are `OverloadedFunction.java`, `FGenericFunction.java`, `GenericFunctionOrMethod.java`, `GenericConstructor.java` and, under the decided items, `MakeInferenceSpecific.java` and `types/FType.java` (`CLIMB-BATCH-7.md`, rung W, "Files it may touch"). So the order becomes: batch 6.5b lands (gathering now); batch 7b; batch 8 with Q-lib in its library work beside R9; the checker at a true zero; the switch-over; Q-walk as a rung of the batch that gives walk the checker's static types, or the one after. Batch N's second run as recorded is retired, and its record's section 1 says so in one paragraph; rows 79, 443, 437's walk half and 486 move to Q-walk's line in `PLAN.md`; row 454's integer half closes on the compiled path with Q-lib; item 33 and row 517 close with Q-lib.

### 4.8 What could go wrong

- The switch-over's "walk takes the checker's static types" step is R7's plan and is not designed. If it is cut, or comes late, Q-walk needs option 1's full set at that time. The cost then is option 1's cost now, and nothing built meanwhile is lost: Q-lib is needed under every shape.
- Q-lib's expected zero change to walk's outputs rests on the reading that no `IntLiteral` value reaches the library under walk save a numeral below -2^63. The rung's comparison over the 440 tests is the check; a changed output is listed, and a numeral below -2^63 in a test would be the first place to look.
- Row 432 (`SUM <|1, 2, 3|>`) stays open under both halves: the probe found it refused under the switch too, over `ArrayList[\IntLiteral\]`, because `IntLiteral` carries no additive algebra. Whether Q-lib gives `IntLiteral` the algebra every flat number type carries is the rung's choice to list, not this judgement's; the row is not on microGPT's path.
- Item 33's `CMP` per type was measured on the checker for `ZZ32` only (61 and 43 errors gone); the other integer types' `CMP` and the ten `MAXNUM`/`MINNUM` declarations are decision 2's device by reading. The rung's distance capture is their measure.

## For Pavol

**The question.** Rung Q was to give walk the numeral's own type now, and the probe shows walk cannot follow it without static types: do we land the library's model in batch 8 and switch walk's numeral after the switch-over, when walk takes the checker's static types?

**Context.**
- Refresher. A numeral is an integer written in a program, such as `3`. Your decision of 2026-09-27: it gets a type of its own, `IntLiteral`, and each number type converts from it, so `x: RR64 = 3` and `u: NN32 = 3` both work and `3` alone is not secretly a `ZZ32`. The specification wanted numerals polymorphic, converted only where used; the team's compiled library built it that way in 2009; the interpreter's library kept a placeholder, "until coercion is implemented". Coercion in walk is implemented since batches 4 and N.
- Probe Q built the switch as a shadow and ran every interpreter test, the demos and both microGPT checks. microGPT: every value unchanged, 40 of 40 both checks. The library's own numeral sites: unchanged. Arithmetic on bare numerals stays exact and unbounded until the first typed use, which is the specification's intent, and R8's question is answered by that measurement.
- What breaks under walk: 24 tests that passed. Six are what the decision intends (three team tests from 2008 that assert a numeral is a `ZZ32`, three where a library declaration typed `Any` takes the numeral, as the compiled path already does). Nine need static types: a list of numerals comes out as a list of `IntLiteral` where the checker would type it from the variable or parameter it goes into. Walk has no such types; that is the same limit you accepted on 2026-09-29 for walk's coercions, "one now and two after the switch". The rest are small walk gaps with a device each.
- The library half is different: it changes no walk output by reading, costs the checker nothing (4 errors fewer once `ZZ32` states its comparisons on itself), and is needed at the switch-over anyway, when the compiler's own library is deleted.
- The `=` question: a numeral compared with a `ZZ32` must answer correctly; one line in the library does it, unpaid until walk's numeral switches; how fast it should be is a phase-6 question and may be moot once walk takes the checker's coercions.

**Options.**
1. Rung Q widened to every fix now. One large rung, 4M to 8M tokens, walk's inference rewritten to approximate static types, about 5 team test lines in 3 files for your yes, re-measured after 7b changes the same dispatch code, and walk still not matching the checker on lists of numerals.
2. Widen walk's numeral default only. One method; measured, 20 of the 24 still fail. Not a shape on its own.
3. Split by what needs static types. Q-lib, the library's `IntLiteral` model with its coercions, `ZZ32`'s comparisons and item 33's declarations, in batch 8 beside R9's coercion: about 1M tokens, no team test line, no walk change expected. Q-walk, walk's numeral switched with the team tests restated, after the switch-over's step that gives walk the checker's static types: about 2M tokens then, about 5 team test lines then. Batch 7b goes next, since nothing of Q-lib shares a file with it.

**A yes to 3 commits you to:** the numeral's own type in the library now and in walk later, at the point you already set for walk's coercions; batch 7b next, then 8 with Q-lib; rows 79, 443 and 437's walk half staying open until Q-walk; the three team tests untouched until then; batch N's second run as recorded retired.

**A no costs:** under option 1, 4M to 8M tokens and your review of team test lines now for a walk that still differs from the checker; under holding rung Q as recorded, the run cannot land, since it meets the record's own stops, and 7b waits behind it for no reason.

**Recommendation:** option 3 as split here; batch 7b next; Q-lib in batch 8; Q-walk after the switch-over.

<!-- The recheck of `judgement.md` (2026-09-29, `9172ab41f`) against the full text of Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu, "Polymorphic Symmetric Multiple Dispatch with Variance", PACMPL 3 (POPL 2019), article 11, 28 pages, read whole from `research/decks/popl19w.txt` (pdftotext of `research/decks/popl19w.pdf`; both gitignored, neither committed).
